title: Genomic and functional adaptations in the guanylate-binding protein GBP5 highlight specificities of bat antiviral innate immunity
experiments_summary:
1. Transcriptomic analysis: Primary fibroblast-like cells derived from wing punches of three Myotis yumanensis individuals were stimulated with universal type I IFN (1,000 U/mL) or mock for 6 hours. Total RNA was extracted, mRNA-enriched libraries prepared, and sequenced on Illumina NextSeq 500 (paired-end 78 bp). Reads were processed with FASTQC, FASTP, mapped with Salmon and STAR to the M. yumanensis genome, and differential expression analyzed with DESeq2. Results were compared to a published interferome dataset (Shaw et al. 2017) covering six other mammalian species treated under similar conditions.

2. Phylogenomic and positive selection analyses: GBP5 homologs were retrieved from 536 mammalian genomes using miniprot, aligned with MACSE and PRANK, and a maximum-likelihood phylogenetic tree built with IQ-TREE. A total of 348 coding sequences across 11 mammalian orders were analyzed. BUSTED was used for gene-wide positive selection tests per mammalian order; aBSREL identified lineage-specific episodic selection; and site-specific selection was identified using MEME, FUBAR, and FEL from the HyPhy package. Gene duplications, indels, and early stop codons were identified through alignment and phylogenetic inspection.

3. De novo GBP5 sequencing: GBP5 mRNA sequences from Myotis auriculus, M. occultus, M. thysanodes, M. yumanensis, and Eptesicus fuscus cells were obtained by RT-PCR using species-specific primers and Q5 High-Fidelity Polymerase, followed by gel purification and Sanger sequencing. IFN-treated E. fuscus cells were used to confirm early stop codon presence in endogenous transcripts.

4. Subcellular localization assays: Ten bat GBP5 orthologs (plus human GBP5 wild-type and C583A mutant) were cloned with an HA tag into a eukaryotic expression vector. TZM-bl human cells or E. fuscus bat cells were transfected and fixed 48 hours post-transfection. Confocal immunofluorescence microscopy was performed using anti-HA and anti-TGN46 antibodies. Colocalization and TGN-fraction quantification were performed using Cellpose segmentation, ImageJ macros, and the BIOP JACoP plugin on Zeiss LSM 980 AiryScan or LSM 800 images.

5. HIV-1 restriction assays: HEK-293T cells were co-transfected with an HIV-1 genome plasmid (LAI-ΔEnv-Luc2), NL4.3 Env, HIV-1 Rev, and increasing doses of GBP5 (0–4 µg) or empty vector. Supernatant viral particles were quantified by RT-qPCR (using MS2 RNA template and purified RT standard), normalized to 30 mU RT, and used to infect HeLaP4P5 cells. Luciferase activity was measured 72 hours post-infection. Viral and cellular proteins (Gag p55/p41/p24, Env gp160/gp120, HA-GBP5, tubulin, β-actin) were analyzed by western blot from cell lysates and sucrose cushion-purified virion supernatants. Cell viability was assessed by CellTiter-Glo ATP assay.

6. Pseudovirus restriction assays (VSVg and EBLV-1g): HEK-293T cells were co-transfected with LAI-ΔEnv-Luc2, VSVg or EBLV-1g envelope plasmids, and 2 µg GBP5 or empty vector. Supernatants were collected and normalized by RT-qPCR (50 mU RT), and used to infect HEK-293T target cells. Luciferase activity was measured 72 hours post-infection.

7. Site-directed mutagenesis and ancestral CaaX reconstruction: The early stop codon in E. fuscus GBP5 was replaced with the ancestral arginine codon using QuikChange Lightning Site-Directed Mutagenesis. The reconstructed E. fuscus GBP5-CaaX was tested in subcellular localization (TZM-bl and E. fuscus bat cells by confocal microscopy) and in HIV-1, VSVg, and EBLV-1g restriction assays as described above.

8. VSV-GFP infection in bat cells: E. fuscus immortalized fibroblasts were seeded and transfected with 2 µg of empty vector, human GBP5, E. fuscus GBP5, E. fuscus GBP5-CaaX, or M. yumanensis GBP5 plasmids. Thirty-two hours post-transfection, cells were infected with equal volumes of VSV-GFP stock. Sixteen hours post-infection, cells were fixed and analyzed by flow cytometry (MacsQuant) to quantify GFP-positive infected living cells and cell death. Statistical analyses used nested t-tests for immunofluorescence data and one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's test for all other comparisons.
